name: Grenadine
label: Simple Machines
lede: Two label owners and a trombonist set down their day bands and made crooning, cocktail-hour pop built around Goya foods.

eras.title: Three scenes, one lounge act
eras.text: Mark Robinson of Unrest, Jenny Toomey of Tsunami and Rob Christiansen of Eggs each worked inside the DC-area indie world. Grenadine was the side project where none of them had to sound like their day bands.

years.big: Indie-lounge-pop, with comparisons to Rudy Vallee
yt: Robinson and Toomey look back, Discograffiti podcast
years.h: Robinson, Toomey and Christiansen start a lounge act
years.p: Wikipedia dates the start to 1991. Robinson and Toomey sing and play guitar, while Christiansen plays trombone, guitar and drums.
years.xp: Robinson ran Teenbeat and fronted Unrest, Toomey co-ran Simple Machines and sang in Tsunami, and Christiansen played in Eggs. Trouser Press and Wikipedia describe the sound as indie-lounge-pop, a crooning cocktail act that drew comparisons to Rudy Vallee.

years.h: Triology arrives on both Robinson's and Toomey's labels
years.p: The debut single came out on Teenbeat and Simple Machines together, a two-label split the band kept for its whole run.

eras.title: Goya, with a producer from Shimmy Disc
eras.text: Kramer produced the first album, and the trio built an aesthetic around Goya foods. Trouser Press heard it as the record where the three players blended best.

years.cap: Mark Robinson, Jenny Toomey and Rob Christiansen on a couch
years.h: Kramer produces Goya for three labels at once
years.p: Simple Machines, Teenbeat and Kramer's Shimmy Disc shared the release. Song titles like "Philco" and "Decca" look back to old radios and records.
years.xp:
Trouser Press praised the airiness and clarity Kramer brought, and singled out a cover of a Flamingos song sung in an Art Garfunkel style. It judged the debut the more successful blend of the three players.

Wikipedia dates the album to 1992; Trouser Press lists 1993.

years.h: "Don't Forget the Halo" fills the gap between albums
years.p: The second single came out on Teenbeat and Simple Machines, the same two labels as the first.

eras.title: Nopalitos, then a trombone EP
eras.text: The second round came with a new producer and a moodier band, plus a solo EP for the trombonist.

years.h: Warren Defever of His Name Is Alive produces Nopalitos
years.p: The second album came out on Simple Machines and Teenbeat.
years.xp:
Trouser Press heard more conflict this time, with Robinson's whimsical excursions set against Toomey's darker seriousness, and a cavalier take on an older song. Its verdict: the second shot of Grenadine was one too many.

The Simple Machines band page describes the trio as one that hardly ever played live.

years.h: Rob Christiansen gets his own EP
years.p: Christiansen came out on Teenbeat and Simple Machines the same year as Nopalitos.

eras.title: Last call
eras.text: Simple Machines wound down in 1998, and the band's last show was part of its goodbye party.

years.h: Grenadine plays the Simple Machines goodbye party
years.p: It was the band's final show: a mix of sad songs and upbeat ones, from a band that hardly ever played live. Wikipedia lists 1998 as the year Grenadine ended.
years.xp: The label's own band page says the trio played the party, mixing melancholy songs with pop numbers. Toomey and Kristin Thomson closed Simple Machines that year.
